intro: Step into the Hierapolis Archaeology Museum, in Denizli province, opened in 1984. Look around before you look at the objects: you are inside the vaulted halls of the Roman baths of Hierapolis. Here wait the reliefs taken from the city's theatre, and sarcophagi associated with Lycia and Caria.
history: The museum was installed in 1984 in the vaulted halls of the Roman baths of Hierapolis. Its collection brings together the reliefs taken from the city's theatre, the sarcophagi lifted from its necropolis, and the finds of the other Lycus valley cities, Laodicea and Colossae.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the theatre reliefs, the sarcophagus hall and the small finds — and keep looking up at the Roman bath building itself.
facts: Did you know? The necropolis of Hierapolis is among the largest ancient cemeteries in Anatolia, with over a thousand tombs along two kilometres, and most of the sarcophagi in the museum came out of it. Because the museum sits in the vaulted halls of the city's Roman baths, the building is part of the collection too. And the reliefs taken from the theatre's stage building are among the fullest Roman sequences describing the cult of Apollo and Artemis.
outro: This brings our tour of the Hierapolis Archaeology Museum to an end. Before you go, please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash. These works have survived for centuries; let them keep shining for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
